column1: # clues.tsv for ft_split (c-09) — hints only, never answers.
A token is a maximal run of characters that are NOT in the charset. What do the failing inputs have in common, and could yours ever produce a token with no characters in it?

The result is a NULL-terminated array of freshly allocated strings. How many slots does it need, counting the one that marks its end, and can you know that number before you allocate it? What marks the end, so the caller knows where to stop?
You must not modify the input string. Compare it before and after the call: which bytes changed, and which line of your code wrote them?
Nothing in the subject says how many words the string holds. Does anything in your function stop working when there are more of them than in the strings you tried?
